TRIAGED 2026-09-11 (SEC-TENANT-002): the two genuine cross-tenant writes found here are FIXED and gone from this list - mfa admin reset and rbac assign-role both took a target user id straight off the request. What remains is three shapes, none of them a defect but none of them provable by this script either. (1) blog-pipeline and blog-jobs, 12 entries: an internal job runner writing to a run or job row it has already claimed. (2) knowledge-base ratings, votes, bookmarks and reading-history, 5 entries: each preceded by a select filtered on user_id, which is a tighter boundary than tenant, but further back than the 1800-character lookback sees. (3) public-booking, 4 entries: an UNAUTHENTICATED flow where the row is reached by a manage token, which is the credential. The rest are derivations of the same kind - lead-assignment increments a rule it just matched, pipeline-config marks a log row it just read, companies rolls back a row it just created.
